TMNT Frogger: technical notes

How the code works. Line numbers refer to app/src/main/java/com/example/s0/MainActivity.java (559 lines), which holds all the game logic. Player.java, Vehicle.java and GamePad.java are empty classes.

Build set-up

Setting Value Where
Android Gradle Plugin 7.4.1 build.gradle
Gradle 7.5 gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties (the wrapper JAR is not committed)
compileSdk / targetSdk 32 app/build.gradle
minSdk 27 (Android 8.1) app/build.gradle
Java source level 1.8 app/build.gradle
Libraries appcompat 1.4.0, material 1.4.0, constraintlayout 2.1.2 app/build.gradle

app/build.gradle switches on view binding, but the code looks views up with findViewById.

Tests

app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/s0/ExampleInstrumentedTest.java has 40 tests, grouped by sprint (2 to 5): goal bounds, vehicle bounds, the water score checks and username checks. A comment above each test names the group member who wrote it. Each test mocks MainActivity with Mockito and only stubs one of its methods (when(...).thenReturn(...)); none calls the real method or asserts anything, so they do not check the game code. They are instrumented tests: gradle connectedDebugAndroidTest runs them on a connected device or emulator.

Screens

The app has one activity. Each screen is a layout that MainActivity loads with setContentView, and the layouts call its public methods through android:onClick.

activity_main.xml       title                    Start   -> startConfig()
        |
configuration.xml       username, difficulty,    PLAY    -> startGame()  (checks all three are set)
        |               turtle
activity_game_screen.xml                                  -> gamePlay()   (starts the timers)
        |
        +-- all lives lost ----> game_over.xml   Restart -> startConfig()   Exit -> exitGame()
        +-- goal reached ------> game_win.xml    Restart -> startConfig()   Exit -> exitGame()
  • Set-up (lines 100–193): ENTER rejects an empty or whitespace-only username; PLAY refuses to start until a username, a difficulty and a turtle are chosen, and says which is missing.
  • Lives (lines 209–221): Easy 5, Medium 3, Hard 1.
  • exitGame (lines 516–519) calls finish() and then System.exit(0).

Game loop

Two java.util.Timers drive the game. Their tasks post work to the UI thread through a Handler.

  • Player (lines 250–255, 334–366): every 10 ms, changePos moves the turtle 4 pixels in each direction whose arrow is held, kept within x = 2 to 970 and y = 180 to 1870. The arrow buttons set the direction flags in onTouch (lines 368–395) on press and clear them all on any other touch event, such as a release or a slide.
  • Vehicles and logs (lines 294–331): moveObject gives every vehicle and log its own task on the second timer, every 6 ms. Each tick moves the view by its lane speed in pixels. A view that leaves the range x = −500 to 1350 jumps back to the far side. For vehicles, the same tick runs the collision check.

Lanes (constants at lines 32–49, set-up at lines 257–290; a negative speed moves left):

Lane y Speed (pixels per 6 ms) Objects
Road 1 1600 −1 2 cars
Road 2 1480 +1 bus, construction truck, pickup truck
Road 3 1330 −2 trash truck, car
Road 4 1180 +3 pickup truck, government car
Road 5 1030 −3 car, 2 police cars
River 1 720 −1 2 logs
River 2 590 +1 2 logs
River 3 460 −2 2 logs
River 4 330 +3 2 logs

Starting x positions come from eleven slots, 0 to 1200 pixels in steps of 120 (lines 50–60).

Collisions, score and lives

  • Vehicles (lines 457–486): the turtle is a box 40 pixels wide and 54 high around its position; a vehicle is 70 × 40. An overlap calls loseLife.
  • Score (lines 397–411): a step up scores only if it takes the turtle higher than it has been since its last life began; it scores 2 inside the river's rows, 1 elsewhere.
  • Losing a life (lines 488–514): the score goes back to 0 and the turtle back to the start. At 0 lives both timers stop and the game-over screen shows the score.
  • Winning (lines 441–454, 521–531): once the turtle is more than 100 pixels above the bottom edge of the goal strip, both timers stop and the win screen shows the score.

Known gaps

  • The river is not a hazard. checkTouchingWater (lines 428–439) is never called, and the log check and its call are commented out (lines 309–317, 533–558). Logs move, but the turtle can walk across the water.
  • Fixed pixel positions. Lanes, limits and collision boxes are pixel values, not scaled to the screen size.
  • Timers outlive the screen. Nothing stops the timers when the activity pauses; they stop only when the game ends.
  • Unused click handlers. The arrow buttons in activity_game_screen.xml name onLeftTouch, onUpTouch, onDownTouch and onRightTouch, which do not exist. They never fire, because onTouch consumes every touch.
  • Unused strings. strings.xml keeps 20 strings that nothing uses, among them a "MyStack App" set and frog colours. The app's launcher name is S0.
